name: Adrián Hernández Padrón
location: Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Islas Canarias, España
summary: AI Engineer who builds LLM agents and ML systems that act on real data, and measures whether they work. I designed and built Travel Ruter end to end, an AI travel product with a tool-calling agent, MCP servers, decision models and an evaluation harness that gates every change. At Intelequia I lead the Data Science team, building an agent harness that sets up our data platform projects and an anomaly detection system for 556 connected machines that pairs physics-informed ML with LLM incident triage and reporting; at DISA I shipped the first GenAI use cases and a Kubernetes microservices platform for route optimization. Physicist by training, based in Tenerife and open to remote work or relocation.

highlights: Lead a 4-person Data Science team: solution architecture, code and model review, and the call between classical ML and LLM agents for each problem.

Built an agent harness that sets up the team's data platform projects on Microsoft Fabric: it creates the reference architecture, takes project-specific extensions and configures each setup stage so the next one starts ready. New project setup went from weeks to one day.

Built a predictive-maintenance anomaly detection system for an HVAC manufacturer's fleet of 556 connected heat-recovery units, on 4 years of minute-level telemetry: physics-derived features, change-point regime segmentation, a deterministic rule engine, a Ridge plus gradient boosting thermal model bounded by the second law of thermodynamics (fleet median MAE 0.24 °C) and an Isolation Forest, combined into decision logic that flags each incident; an LLM layer then categorizes each incident into a failure family (icing, fouling, sensor drift, fan, bypass, airflow imbalance) and writes the maintenance report.

Turned 18,965 raw anomaly episodes into 4,415 prioritized incidents (about 10 red alerts a week across 452 active units), removed 96.4% of false bypass alerts, and stress-tested it with a 30-week walk-forward simulation that doubled sensor-drift detection from 43% to 86%; daily batch at about 420 ms per unit, tracked in MLflow.

Designed and deployed end to end a retrieval-augmented ML system for construction budgets: semantic search in Qdrant finds similar past work items from a free-text description, and their materials feed the models that assign materials, quantities and prices, behind an API with a custom UI.

Designed and built v2 of the logistics route optimization platform as microservices on Kubernetes with ArgoCD GitOps (routing engine, CVRPTW optimizer with cluster-constrained models, backend, frontend, database, FastAPI service integrated with SAP), cutting route generation time by 30%.
Re-engineered the training and prediction pipeline for about 1,000 models: memory-efficient data loading and parallel execution took the full run from 24 h to 1.5 h and halved compute usage.

Delivered DISA's first GenAI use cases: a sentiment analysis service and LLM workflows that replaced manual review steps, plus research on a RAG assistant over internal documents; owned prompt iteration and answer validation.
Led the MLOps practice for a 4-person team: containerized training and inference, MLflow tracking, model registry and lineage, drift monitoring with rollback.
Led a joint R&D project with the University of La Laguna on anomaly detection in authentication logs (embeddings, sequential models, autoencoders).
